arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: Mr. Rothfeld argued the Philippines waived immunity by participating in U.S. litigation. He stated the lower court ignored sovereign immunity principles. He claimed the Philippines would lose on statute of limitations grounds.

Mr. Swift argued no adequate alternative remedy exists for human rights victims. He stated the Philippines has no remedy in either country. He emphasized the lack of effective legal recourse for victims.

Mr. Kneedler argued sovereign immunity must weigh heavily in jurisdictional decisions. He stated that immunity from suit is a critical factor. He contended the court must respect the sovereign status of the Philippines.

sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: The Philippines argues U.S. courts lack jurisdiction over its sovereign property. It claims Marcos stole these assets while president. the opposing sides argue U.S. courts can settle ownership disputes. They claim the Philippines waived immunity by participating in the case. The core conflict involves competing claims to the same assets.

sections.heading: Why it matters
paragraphs: This case determines whether sovereign immunity bars U.S. courts from resolving property disputes involving foreign governments. It defines the scope of U.S. judicial power over foreign state assets. It impacts how nations protect stolen property abroad. It clarifies the balance between sovereign dignity and private rights.
